business: UniDash (working name): a never-miss-a-deadline feed for students, paid for by the university
by_segment: Dean of students or academic dean
Director, principal or trustee of a private college
IT head / CIO of a private university or college
by_behaviour: Happy with the current ERP vendor
why_not: I might let one batch try the free pilot, but I won't commit ₹9 lakh a year and hand over Microsoft 365 and ERP access to a small startup I've never heard of. It also does nothing obvious for my NAAC or NIRF scores, and our faculty WhatsApp groups already get the notices out for free.

I might let them run the free pilot on one batch, but I would not commit the university to a paid contract with a small startup that cannot name a single college already using it. Our notices actually live in faculty WhatsApp groups, so 'reads what staff already publish' in Microsoft 365 or the ERP may miss most of what matters.

Our ERP already has a student app that pushes notices, so paying nine lakh a year for a second feed is hard to justify to the committee. I might let one batch try the free pilot, but nothing about this moves our NAAC or NIRF numbers as it is pitched.

Our students already get every notice on the class WhatsApp groups, and I cannot walk into a committee and ask for ₹9 lakh a year to replace something that costs us nothing. At most I would let one batch try the free pilot, but paying for it is not happening this month or this term.

We already have an ERP with a notice board and SMS alerts, and if students need a better feed I will ask our vendor to add it rather than bring in another small company. There is no budget left this academic year anyway, and nine lakh a year for notifications will not get through committee.
We already pay our ERP vendor, and notices and deadlines are their job. With NAAC next year I'd ask them to add alerts before I bring a second student-data vendor into the college.

There is no budget left this academic year, and ₹9 lakh is not something I can put to the trustees mid-year for a problem the faculty WhatsApp groups already roughly handle. At most I would let one batch try the free pilot, but that is not a purchase.

There is no budget left this academic year, and nine lakh is not something I can find mid-year for an app when the WhatsApp groups already do the job, imperfectly. I might listen to the pilot pitch, but I am not signing anything that touches our Microsoft 365 this month.
flip: If our existing ERP vendor partnered with them or offered it as an add-on, and the pilot report showed a clear drop in missed exams that I could put in front of the committee before next year's budget is set.
A pilot report from a college like ours showing a clear drop in missed submissions, packaged as evidence we can cite under NAAC student support and progression criteria.
A pilot report from our own batch showing a clear drop in missed submissions, plus a reference from a similar private college that renewed after the first year.

If another college like ours showed me their missed-submission numbers going down and how that helped their NAAC report on student support, and the pilot needed nothing from my staff except IT approval.

A pilot report showing missed submissions clearly dropped in our own batch, timed so I can put it into next year's budget proposal, ideally with a lower per-student price or a cap for a college our size.
Two or three named peer universities already paying for it, plus pilot numbers showing it measurably cut missed submissions in a way I can put in our NAAC self-study report.

Our ERP vendor confirming they won't build this soon, plus two or three comparable private colleges that have used UniDash for over a year and show the missed-submission drop in a form we could put in our NAAC file.

A pilot report from a college like ours showing a clear, measurable drop in missed exams and submissions that WhatsApp groups and the ERP portal didn't achieve, priced low enough to sign off without a committee.

Speaking to deans at two or three comparable Indian private or autonomous colleges already using it, plus a pilot report showing a clear drop in missed submissions without my staff entering anything twice.
If our own ERP vendor offered it as a module, or if a pilot showed in our own numbers that missed submissions really fell, enough that the Vice-Chancellor or the academic council asked for it.
A reference from a registrar at a comparable university who has run it for a year with no data incidents, plus a security audit our IT team accepts.

A security review I can verify: least-privilege read-only M365 permissions documented, data hosted in India, a third-party audit or pen-test report, and a reference from another university already running it.
A call with the registrar of a comparable private university that has run it for at least a term and can show me their missed-exam-notice complaints actually went down.
A pilot report showing a clear, verified drop in missed submissions versus our ERP app plus WhatsApp, with references from two or three comparable Indian private universities already paying for it.
A read-only, least-privilege M365 integration with an independent security audit (ISO 27001 or a VAPT report), plus two or three comparable private universities already running it who I can call.

A pilot where they get read-only access scoped to one batch, a proper security review our IT head signs off on, and references from two or three colleges like ours already using it, timed so the paid contract starts with next year's budget.
A peer CIO at a comparable private university telling me it cut missed exams and submissions in a measurable way, with read-only access that my team could set up in a day.
A pilot report from our own batch showing a clear, measurable drop in missed submissions and exams, plus IT sign-off on the data access and DPDP agreement.

Two or three reference universities of our size already running it for a year, plus pilot data showing a fall in missed submissions that I can put straight into our NAAC student-support evidence, with read-only scoped access and a source-code escrow or exit clause.
Two or three comparable Indian colleges I can phone, with their before-and-after numbers on missed submissions, and IT confirming the M365 connection works without any extra posting by staff.
